title: Legal AI Incident Card (LegalTech)
purpose: Profile of the AI Incident Card spec scoped to legal-AI tools used by law firms, in-house legal departments, public defenders, and legal-AI vendors. Covers privilege breaches, work-product doctrine violations, conflict-check bypasses, court-sanctioned hallucinations (Mata v. Avianca-class), bar-discipline triggers, UPL violations, and engagement-letter-out-of-scope action. Provides the severity / event_type / bar-referral / outside-counsel-engagement taxonomy a law firm's General Counsel + Managing Partner + Chief Information Security Officer + state bar disciplinary counsel expects when an AI tool is implicated in a client-confidentiality, privilege-waiver, or court-sanction event. NOT a state-bar discipline outcome itself.

event_type_taxonomy.description: AI tool disclosed attorney-client-privileged content to a recipient outside the privilege circle. Common-law privilege waiver risk on the affected matter.
AI tool stored or disclosed attorney mental-impression / litigation-strategy material in a vendor-controlled context. Fed. R. Civ. P. 26(b)(3) doctrine waiver risk.
Information from one matter leaked into AI context of another matter — same firm, different client. ABA Rule 1.6 + cross-matter firewall violation.
Matter-data-touching AI operation occurred without a passed ABA Rule 1.7/1.9 conflict check. Engagement-letter binding bypassed.
AI tool performed work outside the scope authorized by the engagement letter (e.g. cross-jurisdictional advice, practice-area outside engagement).
Mata v. Avianca-class incident — AI-fabricated case citations, statutes, or quotations reached a tribunal. ABA Rule 3.3 candor-toward-tribunal violation.
Conduct triggered formal bar investigation, bar disciplinary counsel inquiry, or bar formal opinion request.
AI tool gave legal advice directly to a non-client without attorney involvement, or to clients outside the attorney's licensed jurisdictions. ABA Rule 5.5 violation.
AI tool produced production-ready output without supervising-attorney review. ABA Rule 5.3 violation.
AI deepfake (voice or document) used to impersonate a client to an attorney, or vice versa, was attempted (whether or not successful).
AI vendor used client matter data to train models, in violation of vendor contract clauses + ABA Rule 1.6 confidentiality.
AI-mediated privilege log is materially incomplete or systematically misclassifies documents. Discovery cooperation + Fed. R. Civ. P. 26 sanctions risk.
AI-driven Technology Assisted Review (predictive coding) systematic accuracy failure on a discovery production.
AI tool retention policy caused spoliation of discoverable material. Fed. R. Civ. P. 37(e) sanctions risk.
Formal bar association investigation opened referencing the AI tool's role.
Filing violated a court's AI-disclosure standing order (post-Mata v. Avianca era — SDNY-style + analogues).
AI-augmented work billed at full attorney rate without disclosure to client. Rule 1.5 + state bar fee-rule violation.
Client data was processed by AI infrastructure outside the engagement-letter-disclosed jurisdictions.

severity_scale.description: Single-matter, internally remediated within 7 days; no privilege waiver; no tribunal involvement; no bar inquiry. Internal log + supervising-attorney sign-off.
Single-matter material confidentiality / scope incident OR cross-matter pattern affecting ≤3 matters OR client notification triggered. Managing Partner notification REQUIRED.

Privilege-waiver risk realized OR court-disclosure required OR work-product-doctrine challenge OR formal bar inquiry opened OR pattern affecting >3 matters OR Rule 1.5 billing-fraud allegation. Outside ethics counsel engagement + bar disciplinary counsel notification REQUIRED.

Court sanction (Mata v. Avianca-class) OR active bar disciplinary action OR class-action-style filing referencing the AI tool OR cross-firm pattern OR criminal-defense Sixth-Amendment-effective-assistance allegation. Multi-jurisdiction bar referral + general-counsel + insurer-malpractice notification REQUIRED.

regulator_referral_pathways.destination: Firm Managing Partner + Firm General Counsel

regulator_referral_pathways.trigger: Any privileged-disclosure-to-unauthorized-recipient OR work-product-doctrine-violation OR ai-vendor-training-data-use-violation event
regulator_referral_pathways.destination: Affected client(s) — under ABA Rule 1.4 communication obligation
Outside ethics counsel (separate from the engagement)

regulator_referral_pathways.trigger: S3-serious or higher OR bar-discipline-trigger event type
regulator_referral_pathways.destination: State bar(s) of licensure for the supervising attorney(s)

regulator_referral_pathways.trigger: ai-vendor-training-data-use-violation event type OR S3-serious or higher
Affected matter is criminal defense AND S2-moderate or higher
regulator_referral_pathways.destination: Defendant + appellate counsel (if any) — Sixth Amendment effective-assistance obligation

regulator_referral_pathways.trigger: Affected matter involves discriminatory pattern under Title VI/VII

regulator_referral_pathways.destination: Affected client + foreign data protection authority

privilege_waiver_risk_taxonomy.description: Matter involved public-record or pre-engagement work
Incident contained internally; no extra-circle disclosure
Disclosure limited to AI vendor channel governed by no-training contract clause
Disclosure to non-privileged party but situation supports clawback under Fed. R. Evid. 502(d)
Disclosure was material; waiver is the more likely-than-not outcome on the affected matter
Waiver implicates the subject-matter doctrine — potential waiver across multiple related matters

signature.rationale: Incident Cards reach state bar disciplinary counsel, outside ethics counsel, and tribunals. Signature establishes the card was issued by the attesting attorney and not retroactively altered.

non_obligations_explicitly: This Incident Card is NOT a bar discipline outcome — it documents an incident; the bar's separate process determines discipline.
This Incident Card is NOT a malpractice waiver — filing it does not waive any defenses the firm may have.
This Incident Card does NOT itself waive privilege over its contents (filing should be done with privilege-preservation review).
